content.text:
I submitted index 10 (Ba 0.528, Mn 0.472) as the best composition. It gave 5.46e-5 A, the highest of the three merit measurements I was allowed.

| Index | Ba fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.61 | 0 A |
| 8 | 0.50 | 3.3e-6 A |
| 10 | 0.53 | 5.46e-5 A (about 16x index 8) |

- **Why index 10:** it sits just on the Ba-rich side of BaMnO3. The models predict BaMnO3 is stable with a band gap of 2.73 eV, and the nearby phase Ba6Mn5O16 has a gap of about 2 eV. So a mix of the two should absorb the 3.22 eV light.
- **Mn-rich side (Ba below about 0.45):** not measured. The phases predicted there have very small band gaps (0.34 eV for Ba2Mn3O8, 0.89 eV for BaMn4O8), which makes them poor photoanodes. This rests on predictions only.
- **Ba-rich side:** I picked index 14 because Ba3Mn2O8 is predicted to have a 3.07 eV gap, but it gave no photocurrent.

With only three measurements, I can't tell whether the true peak is at index 10 or at a nearby composition I didn't measure, such as index 9 or 11. I used one of the five XRD measurements (index 14), and its pattern didn't match any known phase well.
